Hon'Ble Sandeep Jain, J. 
1.
Sri Shailesh Upadhyay, learned counsel for the appellant and Sri Shivam Yadav, learned counsel for NOIDA are present.

2. The instant first appeal under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 has been filed by the landowner against the Award and Decree dated 14.05.2001 passed by the Court of First Additional District Judge, Ghaziabad in LAR No. 316 of 1997, Indrapal v. State of U.P., whereby for the acquired land situated in Village Naurangabad Khadar, District- Ghaziabad, now Gautam Buddha Nagar, which was acquired for the NOIDA, compensation at the rate of Rs. 200/- per sq. yard,
besides other statutory benefits, admissible under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 has been awarded to the landowner for land acquired through notification under Section 4(1) of the Act dated 15.02.1992.

entities.text: Court of First Additional District Judge, Ghaziabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that in similar land acquisition matters relating to the same village and same notification, the other landowners had challenged the Award of the Reference Court by filing First Appeal No. 298 of 2015 (Bhawar Singh v. Noida & Another) which was allowed by the Division Bench of this Court vide order dated 18.05.2015, whereby compensation at the rate of Rs. 340/- per sq. yard besides other statutory benefits admissible under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 was awarded to the landowners, which was challenged by the landowners by filing Special Leave Petition (Civil) Diary No. 618 of 2021 which was dismissed by the Apex Court on 22.10.2021.

entities.text: Special Leave Petition (Civil) Diary No. 618 of 2021
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: Learned counsel submitted that since the matter has attained finality from the Apex Court, as such, appellant is also entitled to get compensation at the rate of Rs. 340/-per sq. yard regarding his acquired land situated in Village Naurangabad Khadar, District- Ghaziabad, now Gautam Buddha Nagar.

4. Per contra, Shri Shivam Yadav, learned counsel representing the NOIDA very fairly conceded that the Division Bench of this Court has awarded compensation at the rate of Rs. 340/- per sq. yard vide it's order dated 18.05.2015 which was not challenged by the Authority before the Apex Court but learned counsel submitted that the appellant may not be granted interest on the enhanced amount of compensation awarded by this Court for the period during which the appeal remained defective on account of non-payment of court fees and remained dismissed for want of prosecution.
5. I have heard learned counsel for both the sides and perused the record.

6. It is apparent that in the instant appeal, the matter relates to acquisition of land situated in Village Naurangabad Khadar, District- Ghaziabad, now Gautam Buddha Nagar, which was acquired vide notification under Section 4(1) of the Act dated 15.02.1992, the possession of the land was taken on 31.03.1994 and the Award of the Collector was made on 12.08.1996 whereby compensation at the rate of Rs. 54.54 per sq. yard was awarded to the landowners besides other statutory benefits admissible under the Land Acquisition Act, which has been enhanced by the Reference Court vide impugned Award and Decree dated 14.05.2001 to Rs. 200 per sq. yard.

sentences.text:
It is also apparent that regarding similar land acquisition matters regarding the same village and same notification under Section 4(1) of the Act, the other landowners had previously challenged the Award of the Reference Court by filing First Appeal No. 298 of 2015 (Bhawar Singh v. Noida &
Another) which was allowed by the Division Bench of this Court vide order dated 18.05.2015,
whereby compensation at the rate of Rs. 340 per sq. yard besides other statutory benefits admissible under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 was awarded to the landowners, which was challenged by the landowners by filing SLP (Civil) Diary No. 618 of 2021, which was dismissed by the Apex Court vide order dated 22.10.2021.

It is apparent that the matter has attained finality and as such, the appellant is also entitled to get compensation at the same rate as has been awarded by the Division Bench of this Court vide order dated 18.05.2015 for his acquired land situated in Village Naurangabad Khadar, District- Ghaziabad, now Gautam Buddha Nagar.
8.
Accordingly, this appeal is allowed.

The appellant is entitled to get enhanced compensation at the rate of Rs. 340/- per square yard for his acquired land along with 30% solatium, additional compensation @ 12% per annum and interest under Section 28, as provided under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
9.
The instant appeal was filed on 31.08.2001 but the deficiency of the Court fees was made good on 04.02.2003
, as such, the appellant is not entitled to get interest on the enhanced amount of compensation awarded by this Court for the period 31.08.2001 till 04.02.2003.
10. However, in the facts and circumstances of the case, the parties shall bear their own costs.
11. Office is directed to prepare the decree accordingly.
12. All pending application(s), if any, stands disposed of.

(Sandeep Jain,J.) September 26, 2025 Jitendra  Indra Pal vs N.O.I.D.A. And Another on 26 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64171264/
